newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Ethnic violence flares in Timorese enclave.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic violence flares in Timorese enclave.

text.p: Fighting between Catholic Timorese and Muslim Bugis from South Sulawesi flared in the small enclave of Ambeno in East Timor with reports of widespread damage, residents and government officials said.
A report that one person was killed in the violence, which residents said started early on Friday, could not be immediately confirmed.

One resident said more than 80 houses and two mini-buses were burned. Police were not immediately available to confirm the fighting in the former Portuguese enclave, about 200 km (124 miles) west of Dili in Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara province.
Residents said the violence lasted until about midday on Friday as local Timorese attacked ethnic Bugis migrants from South Sulawesi.

Government officials said it was not immediately clear what sparked the fighting but one account said it was linked to disrespect shown to a local Catholic priest who was said to have been served a meal of rice containing chicken bones.

In recent years there has been on-going tension between predominantly Catholic East Timorese and migrants from mostly Moslem Indonesia who dominate the economic life of the former Portuguese colony invaded by Indonesia in 1975.
The United Nations has never recognised Jakarta's annexation of East Timor and still regards Portugal as the administering power.
